answer: In a reputation-based Sybil resistance mechanism, each AI agent is assigned a unique digital identity, like a marble, tied to its real-world verified credentials. As agents interact, they earn reputation tokens that grow in value as they become intertwined in the network, much like a vine. An attacker attempting to create fake identities would need to cultivate an entire virtual garden of convincing agents, requiring significant computational resources and real-world verification to mimic the organic growth of reputation, making large-scale Sybil attacks economically infeasible.
